newsitem.title: USA: Texas cotton harvest makes good progress.
newsitem.headline: Texas cotton harvest makes good progress.

text.p: Harvesting of cotton in the Texas Plains made good progress during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
"Harvest made good progress for most of the week in the Plains with most gins having sizable backlogs of modules," the report said. "Yields continued to be very good in many fields."

Meanwhile, mild, open weather dominated conditions across the state until late in the week, when cold temperatures and a mixture of rain, sleet and snow moved in. Precipitation totals were significant in the Hill Country and south central Texas.
Wheat emerged 100 percent vs 99 week ago, 80 year ago, 83 on a five-year average.
Wheat rated 73 percent of normal, vs 74 w/a, 64 y/a.
Sorghum harvested 97 percent vs 94 w/a, 99 y/a, 98 avg.
Cotton bolls opening 100 percent vs 99 w/a, 98 y/a, 97 avg.
Cotton harvested 69 percent vs 60 w/a, 68 y/a, 67 avg.
Cotton rated 68 percent of normal vs 68 w/a, 57 y/a.
Pasture and range condition was rated 32 percent good to excellent, versus 36 percent at that level last week.
